column1: # Flakes that were fixed in a past commit, so the nightly stress job (ci/stress.sh) can be proved to see one:
# run it on the commit before the fix. `substring of the failing test name<TAB>the fixing commit and what it was`.
# ci/stress-yield.py counts a failure that matches as "known fixed"; every other failure is a new finding.

column2: a7c3f3de (PR 345, base 9f11a68a): the test read the event stream once; the host forwards the failure from its own task; a window of microseconds, 0 of 100 under load, so stress will not see it again
11403e5b (PR 139): the test moved the clock before all 10 000 streams were in; fails 5 of 5 on one CPU with 6 busy loops
dec3bff5 (PR 94): two back-to-back deletes both read the final state; 2 in 4000 runs on two cores

the nightly stress of 2026-10-30 (run 41005460713): the guests wait was 30 s of wall clock over about 7 s of CPU work, and the bystander bar a fixed 5 s; both failed on one CPU with 12 busy loops (6 on a slower runner); the waits now follow the guests' progress and the machine
